sentences.text: Diagnostics and maintenance for the Greenvale Metro communications-based train control system are organised around prompt event collection, controlled remote access, and traceable engineering decisions.
Each safety-related part records time-stamped events for state changes, command acceptance, rejected commands, communication loss, and local protective actions.
The Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives event streams from fixed and onboard equipment through monitored interfaces that do not allow maintenance traffic to alter train movement authority.
The Maintenance Diagnostic Server uses the checksum log to compare stored braking data identifiers against the expected maintenance baseline for the affected train.
Remote diagnostic sessions are initiated by a Signal Maintenance Engineer and are limited to read-only observation unless an approved maintenance window authorises a specific intervention.
The Cyber Security Officer reviews privileged diagnostic access logs and confirms that remote connections use current credentials and approved encryption settings.
The Line Traffic Controller receives the Route Release Exception List during incident triage and uses it to check whether a release anomaly could affect service recovery decisions.
Marble records controller health, interface state, and fallback mode transitions in a form that can be correlated with adjacent wayside and operations records.
The South District Zone Controller maintains comparable diagnostic coverage so that boundary events can be reviewed without relying on a single source of evidence.
The East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report route command histories, point detection changes, and protective lock status to support failure localisation.
The Atlas Onboard Controller stores onboard fault codes, movement authority acceptance records, propulsion cutback requests, and train interface exceptions for later retrieval.
The Dual Channel Odometer provides distance and speed plausibility information that is retained with trainborne diagnostic records after any odometry disagreement.
The Train Radio Modem records bearer loss, reconnection timing, signal quality indicators, and message retry counts needed to distinguish radio coverage issues from equipment faults.
The Wayside Radio Access Network and Safety Data Communication Network provide communication performance records that are compared with controller logs during network-related investigations.
The Metro Operations Control System displays selected fault summaries to the Line Traffic Controller but does not expose detailed maintenance commands at the traffic control workstation.
A Revenue Train Operator reports observed cab indications, train handling effects, and passenger service impacts using the operational reporting channel defined for degraded service.
Failure triage first establishes whether the condition is safety critical, service affecting, cyber security related, or a maintenance-only defect.

Safety critical failures remain under traffic control coordination until the Line Traffic Controller confirms the operating restriction and a Signal Maintenance Engineer confirms the engineering status.
The Maintenance Diagnostic Server preserves raw events, normalised event records, diagnostic session notes, and file integrity values for post-incident analysis.
Configuration records include software build identifiers, parameter set identifiers, radio configuration versions, interlocking data versions, and approved change references.
The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance maintains certificate and key status records used to verify whether communications faults could be related to authentication or expiry conditions.

The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway are checked when reported symptoms involve timetable-driven routing assumptions or passenger-facing messages rather than train control protection.
The Voice Dispatch Console is included in the evidence scope when verbal instructions, emergency calls, or manual coordination affected the response to an event.
After a reportable incident, retained evidence is frozen under maintenance control, copied to a protected repository, and released only through the agreed engineering investigation process.
